# itakeit

> itakeit is dead simple task tracking in Slack channel threads: a free, self-hosted Slack bot that turns every top-level message in its dedicated Slack channels into a task. People claim a task by reacting 🙋, owners set its status with emoji reactions, and a pinned board in each channel counts the open tasks in each status and lists the oldest ones with their owners.

itakeit runs as one Docker container with a SQLite file, or with Postgres when ITAKEIT_DATABASE_URL (or database_url in config.yaml) is set. It connects to Slack over Socket Mode, so it makes only outbound connections and needs no public URL, ingress or TLS certificate. The messages stay in Slack; the database holds only owners, statuses, timestamps, checklist ticks and each channel's board message ID.

## How it works

- Post a top-level message in a task channel and it becomes a task. The bot replies in its thread with a status card.
- React 🙋 to take the task. Several people can own one task. Removing the reaction hands it back.
- Owners react 👀 investigating, 🚧 in progress, ⛔ blocked or ✅ done. The latest status reaction wins. ✅ removes the task from the board.
- ❓ pings the reporter in the thread. The reporter's reply pings the owners and clears the status.
- Non-owners who react with a status emoji get a private hint to claim first. With status_claims: true, any status reaction makes the reactor an owner instead.
- Lines written as [ ] item in the issue become checkboxes on the status card. Anyone can tick them, and ticking the last one pings the owners, or the reporter if unclaimed, to set ✅.
- Owners who go quiet on a task get a reminder in the thread, repeated every configurable number of hours (default 48) until an owner posts or the status changes.
- Messages posted while the bot was down are not lost: the first reaction on one turns it into a task.
- Emoji are configurable, including custom workspace emoji.

## Setup

1. Create a Slack app from the manifest in the repository (scopes: channels:history, groups:history, channels:read, groups:read, chat:write, reactions:read, pins:write).
2. Generate an app-level token with connections:write (SLACK_APP_TOKEN) and install the app to get the bot token (SLACK_BOT_TOKEN).
3. Set auto_channels: true in config.yaml, create one or more channels and invite the bot to each. Every channel the bot is invited to becomes a task channel with its own tasks and board; removing the bot stops it there. All channels share the same settings.
4. Run the image ghcr.io/nice-pink/itakeit:latest with both tokens in the environment. Run exactly one instance per Slack app; it serves every channel the bot is in. Slack delivers each Socket Mode event to only one connection, so a second instance would miss events.

## Related

- itakeit-agent (https://github.com/nice-pink/itakeit-agent), also by nice-pink: a separate Slack app that claims tasks in the channels itakeit serves (the same channels list, or with auto_channels every channel it is invited to) with 🙋, asks for missing details, and replies in the thread with a proposed fix or the finished work. It runs Claude Code with only the tools and MCP servers the operator allows, and writes can require an approver's reaction. Without tools it can also use the Messages API, OpenAI, Langdock or a self-hosted model such as Qwen.
- itakeit-messenger (https://github.com/nice-pink/itakeit-messenger), also by nice-pink: a separate Slack app that reads messages from Slack channels, HTTP and standard input, asks a model (Claude Code or the Messages API, OpenAI, Langdock, or a self-hosted model such as Qwen through any OpenAI-compatible server) whether each contains a task, and posts the tasks as top-level messages to the channel itakeit serves. It also schedules a thread reminder when a message asks for one.
- Betimation (https://betimation.com), also by nice-pink: advanced and fun team task tracking. Projects and goals race on a live racetrack as tasks close, and the team bets on who finishes first. It has a Slack app too.
